newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes off low, looks to recoup losses.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes off low, looks to recoup losses.

text.p: Gold prices slipped to under $340.00 per ounce in early European business on Thursday after an announcement late Wednesday that Belgium planned to step up its gold coin sales.

By the 0930 GMT fixing, short covering had lifted the market off its floor and prompted dealers to forecast gold re-establishing itself around $340.50-$341.50, where it has been for most of this month.
Bullion fixed at $340.15 compared with $341.60 on Wednesday afternoon.
"There was a bit of an over-reaction to the Belgian coin announcement in New York but there has been good short covering at $339-$340 since then," a dealer said.

Late in the European business day, the Belgian government announced a proposal to sell 26 tonnes a year of its gold reserves in the form of commemorative coins over five years probably beginning in 1999 if parliamentary permission was secured.

Dealers said the reaction of New York demonstrated the current market frailties about the threat of central bank sales, where fear was more significant than substance, according to one market observer.
"It's not a big deal but it is another blow to market sentiment," a dealer said.
Belgium has run down its gold reserves by around 733 tonnes since 1989 to around 596 tonnes currently.
The Hong Kong and Tokyo markets were also easier on the Belgian news but forecasts of a test of $338.00 and the four-year low at $336.65 were not fulfilled.
Silver was unchanged at $4.72/$4.74 but some dealers were looking for a repeat of Tuesday's run up to $4.80.
"Some people think it is undervalued," one dealer said, adding that $4.80 would take some beating in the event of a rise.
Platinum and palladium recovered from lows struck yesterday as dealers came in to cover.
However, market sources said there was no fresh news to warrant buying, and that first deliveries of the year from Russia were still expected early next month.

Dealers said Tiger Management, the U.S. fund believed to have amassed 1.5 million ounces of palladium, had not been successful so far in persuading Japanese consumers to buy from its stocks rather than from Russia.
Platinum was up $7.50 at $415.00/$420.00 and palladium was at $202.00/$206.00, up $13.00. --Brian Spoors +44 171 542 8058
